title: Beethoven’s Fifth, first movement, in four recordings
work: Symphony No. 5 in C minor, Op. 67 — first movement
question: In each of four recordings the conductor sets how long the held notes of the opening motto last.
intro: In November 1913, Arthur Nikisch recorded Beethoven’s Fifth with the Berlin Philharmonic, playing into a recording horn. Odeon’s house orchestra had recorded it two years earlier. Mengelberg’s Concertgebouw and the Skidmore College Orchestra are compared with them here at the first three Gs. Each conductor sets how long the fourth note is held.

recordings.label: Odeon Orchestra, 1911
recordings.note: Odeon’s house orchestra made the first complete recording of a symphony, Beethoven’s Fifth, in Berlin in August 1911.

recordings.label: Arthur Nikisch, 1913
recordings.note: Nikisch took the first movement unusually broadly with the Berlin Philharmonic and left out the exposition repeat.

recordings.label: Willem Mengelberg, 1940
recordings.note: This opening side has Mengelberg with the Concertgebouw Orchestra, which he had led since 1895.

recordings.label: Skidmore College Orchestra
recordings.note: Skidmore takes the exposition repeat, so the horns’ call and the soft E♭ major violin tune are heard twice.

passages.label: Opening motto, repeated
passages.note: Three Gs fall to E♭; three Fs follow and fall to a held D. Beethoven marked fermatas here, and their length is left to the conductor.

passages.label: Rising string passage
passages.note: The strings climb, passing the short rhythm from part to part. Woodwinds and horns answer before the orchestra plays louder.

passages.label: Horn call and second subject
passages.note: A short chord and a pause precede the horns. Their wide call leads into the violins’ soft E♭ major tune.

passages.label: Development
passages.note: The horns, in the familiar rhythm, move down to G; the strings play D♭ against it.

passages.label: Start of the coda
passages.note: The violins hold a high C while the bass changes beneath it. The cadence that would end the movement leads instead into a long coda.
